passage: Nadia heard Dalia's key in the door at nine, two hours late again. Their flat in Lisbon smelled of the soup Nadia had made. Dalia dropped her bag and stood in the hallway, still in her coat, staring at the shoe rack. Nadia had planned to ask about the weekend trip to her own parents' village. She looked at Dalia's grey face and put the question away. 'Soup's warm. Bath's running. You don't have to talk.' Dalia's eyes filled. 'Sorry. I'm useless tonight.' 'You're tired. That's different.' Nadia texted her mother that they might come a week later. Later Dalia fell asleep on the sofa with her head on Nadia's knee. On Saturday morning she woke first and made coffee for them both, humming.

qa.q: What had Nadia made for dinner?
qa.a: Soup.

qa.q: What was Nadia thinking when she saw Dalia's grey face?
qa.a: Nadia felt concerned and decided the weekend question could wait, seeing that Dalia was worn out.

qa.q: Which of Nadia's choices helped most?
qa.a: Offering soup, a bath and no need to talk, and quietly moving the visit, gave Dalia space to recover without guilt.

qa.q: What was it like for Dalia to be met with soup and no questions?
qa.a: Dalia felt guilty and close to tears at first, calling herself useless, but being allowed to rest let her recover and wake up humming.

passage: In the staffroom of the girls' school, Karthik watched Vinita mark the same answer sheet for the third time. She had covered two absent teachers' classes all week and stayed late for the science fair. Now the principal's message pinged: someone was needed to run Saturday's parents' meeting. Vinita reached for her phone to volunteer. Karthik got there first. 'I'll take Saturday,' he typed. Then, to her: 'And give me half those sheets. You're done for today.' Vinita opened her mouth to protest, then laughed weakly and handed them over. 'I owe you.' 'You don't. Go home and sleep.' The next Monday she came in with her usual jokes and a box of homemade laddoos, which she left on his desk without a word.

qa.q: What had Vinita covered all week?
qa.a: Two absent teachers' classes.

qa.q: What was Karthik thinking when Vinita reached for her phone to volunteer?
qa.a: He was worried that she was already exhausted and would overload herself, so he stepped in first.

qa.q: How did Karthik offer practical relief?
qa.a: He took the Saturday meeting and half the marking and told her to go home, without making her feel guilty about it.

qa.q: How did the break seem to affect Vinita?
qa.a: She came back on Monday with her usual jokes and left laddoos for Karthik, which suggests she felt rested and grateful.

grounding: Shows a coworker seeing a colleague depleted and taking tasks off her instead of pushing, and how being allowed to recover strengthens their working bond.

Salma

passage: You want to know what makes a good teammate, so let me, Yamini, tell you about last March. My coworker Salma had just finished a product launch. Six weeks of late nights. The Monday after, she came in with her hair still wet, stared at her screen and couldn't find words for a client email. Our manager wanted her on the next pitch that same week. I remember feeling annoyed at first, because that meant more for me. Then I looked at her properly. So I said, 'I'll take the pitch. Go home at four. No messages from us till Thursday.' She actually cried with relief. And the next month, when I was drowning, she did the same for me without being asked.

passage: I'm Jeevan, and I sit next to Irfan in the bank's back office. I can only tell you what I saw. For three weeks after the system change, Irfan arrived first and left last. His jokes stopped. On Friday he read the same spreadsheet line aloud twice, then just rubbed his eyes for a long time. I don't know what was going on inside him; maybe it wasn't only work. Our team lead started to hand him another file. I said, 'Give it to me. Irfan, go home.' He protested a little, then went. I didn't ask questions or tell anyone. On Monday he brought me a box of sweets and said he had slept most of Saturday.

passage:
Friday: Baljeet came home from a third twelve-hour day at the hospital and sat in the parked car for ten minutes before coming up. Gurpreet saw it from the balcony and felt a pang. At dinner Baljeet barely spoke. Gurpreet had planned to ask about the cousin's wedding trip, and didn't.
Saturday: Gurpreet took the laundry and the vegetable shopping, told the family on the phone they would visit next week instead, and let Baljeet sleep till eleven. No questions, no "you look terrible".
Sunday: Baljeet woke, made chai for both of them and sat close on the sofa. "Thank you for not needing anything from me yesterday. I didn't feel guilty once." Gurpreet smiled. "Now, about that wedding trip..." Baljeet laughed.

qa.q: Until what time did Baljeet sleep on Saturday?
qa.a: Till eleven.

qa.q: What did Gurpreet feel on seeing Baljeet sit in the car for ten minutes?
qa.a: Gurpreet felt a pang of concern, sensing that Baljeet was depleted.

qa.q: Which of Gurpreet's choices gave Baljeet real relief?
qa.a: Dropping the wedding question, taking the laundry and shopping, moving the family visit, and letting Baljeet sleep without comments.

qa.q: How did Baljeet feel about being allowed to rest?
qa.a: Baljeet felt grateful and free of guilt, thanking Gurpreet for not needing anything that day.

grounding: Shows a person who sees someone close depleted and, instead of pushing, offers space and practical relief, so rest comes without guilt and the bond grows.
